This is the paper the draft describes. However, its MONARCH 3 data input was the interim OS analysis (HR 0.754, 5.8 years follow-up), which has since been superseded by the final OS analysis (HR 0.804, 8.1 years, May 2024). A newer Lancet Oncology reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis (Beshr et al., 2026) exists but addresses CDK4/6i vs endocrine therapy alone, not head-to-head drug comparisons.

The final MONARCH 3 OS analysis (May 2024, 8.1 years) gives HR 0.804 (95% CI 0.637–1.015). The point estimate and interval both shifted — the final HR is less favorable for abemaciclib and the CI now crosses 1.0 (non-significant), whereas the interim HR did not cross 1.0. The NMA's conclusion of no significant OS difference between drugs is directionally unchanged, but the underlying MONARCH 3 figure it used is now outdated. The draft does not itself quote the NMA's internal MONARCH 3 HR, so no draft figure is directly wrong, but the NMA it cites as evidence was built on superseded MONARCH 3 data.

objections.objection: The draft states the MONARCH 3 corrigendum is 'behind the publisher's wall' and therefore unread, but the corrigendum is open access under a Creative Commons licence.
objections.quote: A corrigendum to this paper exists — Ann Oncol 2025;36:1556 — and we have not been able to read it: it is behind the publisher's wall.
objections.why: The corrigendum (doi 10.1016/j.annonc.2025.07.002) is published open access under a Creative Commons Attribution–NonCommercial–NoDerivs licence, as shown by the publisher's own page. The draft's disclaimer of access is factually wrong. The corrigendum corrects a figure-4 event count (placebo arm: 162 → 132) and does not appear to affect the HR, CI or p-value the draft relies on — but the draft cannot honestly say it has not read a document that is freely available. A reader who checks will find the corrigendum open and will conclude either that the draft did not look carefully or that the disclaimer is false.
objections.fix: Read the corrigendum (it is open access). If the correction does not affect any figure used on this page, say so positively: 'The corrigendum corrects an event-count label in Figure 4 of the original paper; it does not affect the HR, CI or p-value reported here.' Remove the claim that it is behind a paywall.

objections.objection: The draft says the MONARCH 3 corrigendum has not been checked, then immediately asserts 'we have no reason to think any of them is affected' — a confidence claim that contradicts the stated ignorance.
objections.quote: Every MONARCH 3 figure on this page matches both the original article and the SABCS 2023 presentation of the same analysis, so we have no reason to think any of them is affected, but we have not checked and say so rather than leave the reader to assume we had.
objections.why: The draft simultaneously disclaims having read the corrigendum and asserts a conclusion ('no reason to think any of them is affected') that can only be reached by reading it or by knowing what it corrects. The two halves of the sentence are in tension: if you have not read it, you cannot know whether your figures are affected. The corrigendum in fact corrects a figure-4 event-count label, not the statistical outputs — so the substantive conclusion is correct — but the reasoning as written is self-contradicting.
objections.fix: Since the corrigendum is open access and corrects only a figure label, read it and state the finding directly: 'The corrigendum corrects an event-count label in Figure 4 and does not affect the HR, CI or p-value used here.'

objections.objection: The draft describes the PALOMA-2 missing-data imbalance as something 'they said limits interpretation' and attributes the sensitivity analysis to the investigators, but does not note that the JCO 2024 paper itself was published with errors and carries its own correction notice.
objections.quote: PALOMA-2 is also the trial whose investigators recorded a large and disproportionate imbalance in missing survival data between its arms — survival status was unknown for 13.3% of the palbociclib arm and 21.2% of the placebo arm — which they said limits interpretation.
objections.why: The JCO 2024 PALOMA-2 paper was published with errors and a correction was issued (the paper's own PubMed entry notes it was 'published online January 22, 2024, with errors'). The draft cites this paper as a primary source for the missing-data figures and the sensitivity analysis without noting this. The missing-data percentages and sensitivity-analysis HR appear unaffected by the correction, but the draft's sourcing section does not flag the correction the way it flags the MONARCH 3 corrigendum — creating an inconsistency in how it treats corrections to its two primary sources.
objections.fix: Add a note in the PALOMA-2 sources entry analogous to the MONARCH 3 corrigendum note: acknowledge the correction notice exists, state which figures it affects, and confirm whether the missing-data and sensitivity-analysis figures used here are affected.

objections.objection: The draft presents the 97% interval-overlap figure as though it measures how similar the two drugs' effects are, but interval overlap is a function of sample size and event count, not of effect size — a point the draft makes about p-values but does not apply to this derived statistic.
objections.quote: 97% of ribociclib's interval lies inside abemaciclib's.
objections.why: The draft correctly warns that where an interval ends 'is set by how many patients were enrolled, how many events occurred and how variable they were' — but it applies that warning only to the significance threshold, not to the overlap figure it has just calculated from those same interval bounds. A reader will take '97% overlap' as a measure of how similar the drugs are; it is equally a measure of how wide abemaciclib's interval is, which is itself a function of the trial's power for OS. The figure is not wrong, but it is presented without the same caveat the draft applies to the p-values.
objections.fix: Add a one-sentence caveat after the 97% figure: 'That overlap is also a function of how wide abemaciclib's interval is — itself a consequence of that trial's power for overall survival — not only of how close the point estimates are.'

objections.objection: The draft says 'Survival was a secondary endpoint in all three' trials, but PALOMA-2's OS analysis was powered prospectively with 80% power and a pre-specified event count — a design feature the draft itself describes two paragraphs later — making 'secondary' potentially misleading about its statistical standing.
objections.quote: Survival was a secondary endpoint in all three.
objections.why: The draft correctly distinguishes PALOMA-2 (powered for OS) from MONARCH 3 (not powered for OS) two paragraphs later, but the sentence 'Survival was a secondary endpoint in all three' — offered as a statement about statistical power — flattens that distinction at the moment it introduces it. A reader who stops at that sentence will not know that 'secondary' covers both a powered and an unpowered analysis. The draft repairs this in the next paragraph, but the repair comes after the flattening, not alongside it.
objections.fix: Qualify the sentence on first use: 'Survival was a secondary endpoint in all three — though, as the next paragraph explains, secondary does not mean equally powered.'

objections.objection: The draft says 'no number on this page comes from a news report' in a way that implicitly characterises news reports as a class of unreliable sources, without identifying any specific report or error.
objections.quote: No number on this page comes from a news report, and none from a guideline's summary of a trial.
objections.why: This is a sourcing statement about the draft's own practice, not an accusation against a named outlet. It is close to the line, however: it implies that news reports and guideline summaries are sources from which wrong numbers could come, without citing an instance. As written it is a statement of method rather than a charge, and it does not name anyone — so it does not reach the level of the recorded UNSUPPORTED error. It is worth softening to make clear it is a positive claim about sourcing discipline, not a negative claim about others.
objections.fix: Rephrase as a positive sourcing statement: 'Every figure above traces to a primary trial publication or label, cited by name in the entry below.' Remove the implicit contrast with news reports.

inferences.quote: its cumulative two-sided type I error of 0.05 was divided between the intention-to-treat population and a visceral-disease subgroup, and spent across interim and final analyses under an O'Brien-Fleming spending function
inferences.problem: The description conflates two distinct alpha-reduction operations — a graphical population split (initial allocation 0.04 to ITT, 0.01 to sVD) and an O'Brien-Fleming time-spending function — presenting them as a single mechanism, and 'divided' implies an unspecified or equal split when the actual ratio was 4:1.
inferences.correct_reading: The 0.05 was first allocated between populations by a graphical testing procedure (0.04 to ITT, 0.01 to sVD), and then within each population the cumulative type I error was controlled across interim and final analyses using a Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming spending function; both operations together produced the final ITT boundary of 0.034.
inferences.fix: its cumulative two-sided type I error of 0.05 was first split between the intention-to-treat population and a visceral-disease subgroup by a graphical testing procedure — with an initial allocation of 0.04 to the ITT population and 0.01 to the subgroup — and then spent across interim and final analyses within each population under a Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming spending function

inferences.quote: MONALEESA-2 states a two-sided p of 0.008; what boundary its final analysis was tested against we could not establish, and if it too spent alpha at an interim then its bar also sat below .05
inferences.problem: The ESMO 2021 conference abstract of the same final analysis (same data cutoff, same 400 events) reports P=.004 — half the NEJM figure — which is consistent with the NEJM paper reporting the two-sided value of a one-sided test; this published discrepancy is evidence bearing directly on the boundary question the draft says it cannot resolve, and the draft does not acknowledge it.
inferences.correct_reading: The ESMO 2021 abstract of the same analysis gives P=.004 and the NEJM 2022 paper gives p=0.008; the most parsimonious explanation is that the ESMO figure is one-sided and the NEJM figure is two-sided, which would confirm that the final analysis used a one-sided test and that the boundary sat below 0.025 one-sided — supporting the draft's inference that the bar sat below .05, and providing the sourced evidence the draft says it lacks.
inferences.fix: MONALEESA-2 states a two-sided p of 0.008 in the NEJM publication; the ESMO 2021 abstract of the same analysis gives P=.004, consistent with the NEJM figure being the two-sided equivalent of a one-sided test — which would mean the boundary sat below 0.025 one-sided, and below .05 two-sided. What the prespecified boundary was we could not establish from the publications we could open, but the discrepancy between the two published p-values is itself evidence that alpha was spent at an interim.

best_coverage.got_right: Correctly performed a network meta-analysis of seven phase III RCTs (4,415 patients) and found no statistically significant OS difference between any pair of the three CDK4/6 inhibitors. Explicitly noted the absence of direct comparisons as the reason for the indirect method. Also reported that in the AI-backbone subgroup, palbociclib had a non-significantly worse OS vs ribociclib and abemaciclib (HR 1.26 and 1.19 respectively, both non-significant), preserving the nuance that palbociclib's result is directionally different even if not statistically separable. Reported safety differences (GI toxicity, neutropenia, diarrhea, discontinuation rates) between the three drugs.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not address the NCCN category grading system or explain what the category 1 vs 2A distinction means for clinical practice. Does not discuss the cardiac monitoring burden unique to ribociclib as a countervailing consideration. Does not note that MONARCH 3 OS was a secondary endpoint with limited power, or that the trial's OS analysis was originally planned as part of a pooled analysis with MONARCH 2.

best_coverage.outlet: Annals of Oncology — MONARCH 3 final OS (Goetz et al., May 2024)
best_coverage.got_right: Published the prespecified final OS results for MONARCH 3: HR 0.804 (95% CI 0.637–1.015; P=0.0664, non-significant) after a median follow-up of 8.1 years. Correctly preserved the composite picture — statistically significant PFS benefit (HR 0.535) persisting at final analysis, but OS not reaching significance. This is the definitive source for the MONARCH 3 OS figure the draft uses.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not compare MONARCH 3's OS result to MONALEESA-2's in the context of what the difference in statistical significance means for guideline grading. Does not discuss whether the OS discrepancy between trials reflects drug differences or trial-design differences (power, population, follow-up).

best_coverage.outlet: Flatiron Health / PMC real-world study (published January 2025)
best_coverage.got_right: Largest real-world comparative OS analysis of all three CDK4/6 inhibitors plus AI. Used stabilised inverse-probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW). Found no significant OS differences: ribociclib vs palbociclib aHR 0.98 (P=0.7531), abemaciclib vs palbociclib aHR 0.95 (P=0.4292), abemaciclib vs ribociclib aHR 0.97 (P=0.6956). Sensitivity analyses confirmed findings. Correctly described as the largest such real-world study.
best_coverage.still_omitted: The paper itself frames the absence of RCTs as the reason for the study, using the phrase 'in the absence of RCTs to directly compare' — it does not characterise its own design as a 'direct comparison,' which is a semantic distinction the draft makes but the paper does not. Does not address NCCN category grading or the cardiac monitoring asymmetry.

best_coverage.outlet: ASCO Post — PALOMA-2 OS coverage (August 2022 and February 2024)
best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly reported the missing survival data imbalance (13.3% vs 21.2%) and stated that 'interpretation of these overall survival data was limited' because of it. Also reported the recovered-data analysis (HR 0.92 after data recovery), which the draft does not mention. Correctly identified OS as a secondary endpoint.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not compare the PALOMA-2 OS result to MONALEESA-2 or MONARCH 3 in the context of what the difference means for guideline grading. Does not discuss the statistical power argument — that the OS discrepancy may reflect chance rather than drug differences.

best_coverage.outlet: npj Breast Cancer — power analysis (Jacot et al., 2018)
best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly argued that 'if a significant OS improvement is observed in some but not all trials, this discrepancy might be more attributable to chance than to a truly different drug efficacy.' Calculated that the power of all four trials to demonstrate a statistically significant OS improvement is less than 70% if the OS gain is ≤12 months. Correctly identified OS as a secondary endpoint in all three trials. Noted MONARCH 3's OS analysis was originally planned as a pooled analysis with MONARCH 2, making standalone MONARCH 3 OS results exploratory.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Predates the final OS results from all three trials, so cannot apply the power argument to the actual observed HRs. Does not address the real-world comparative data or the NCCN grading implications.

best_coverage.outlet: ASCO Daily News / ASCO Post — MONALEESA-2 OS and CDK4/6 inhibitor comparison
best_coverage.got_right: Correctly reported MONALEESA-2 OS HR 0.76 (0.63–0.93) as significant and PALOMA-2 HR 0.96 (0.78–1.18) as not significant. Noted MONARCH 3 data were still maturing at time of writing. Explicitly stated 'the reasons why palbociclib has not demonstrated a survival advantage remain unclear' — acknowledging uncertainty rather than asserting drug inferiority. Recommended either ribociclib or abemaciclib over palbociclib as first-line with an AI.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not discuss the overlapping confidence intervals between ribociclib and abemaciclib or what the four-hundredths difference in point estimates means. Does not address the network meta-analysis or real-world comparative data. Does not discuss the cardiac monitoring burden of ribociclib as a countervailing factor.

contradictions.quote: The record that the drugs have not been directly compared in clinical trials is broader than the evidence supports — the real-world cohort is a direct comparison of all three. It is not randomised. It is direct.
contradictions.counterexample: The Flatiron real-world study (PMC11758200) itself uses the phrase 'in the absence of RCTs to directly compare the effectiveness of the three CDK4/6is' as its own framing — the paper does not characterise its design as a 'direct comparison.' The NCCN statement refers to clinical trials; a retrospective observational database study is not a clinical trial by any standard definition, so the guideline's statement is technically accurate as written.
contradictions.fix: Reframe as: 'The guideline's statement is technically accurate — no clinical trial has directly compared the three drugs. What exists is a large real-world observational comparison, which is direct in the sense of comparing the drugs against each other, but is not a clinical trial and is not randomised. The distinction matters and the guideline's language, while narrow, is defensible.'

contradictions.quote: Abemaciclib's hazard ratio is 0.80, on an interval running 0.64 to 1.02.
contradictions.counterexample: The final prespecified OS analysis of MONARCH 3 (Annals of Oncology, May 2024, after 8.1 years median follow-up) reports HR 0.804 (95% CI 0.637–1.015; P=0.0664). The draft's figures (0.80, 0.64–1.02) appear to derive from an interim analysis, not the final OS result. The final upper bound is 1.015, not 1.02, and the lower bound is 0.637, not 0.64. The draft's figures are close but not the final published numbers.
contradictions.fix: Update to the final MONARCH 3 OS figures: HR 0.804 (95% CI 0.637–1.015; P=0.0664, non-significant) after a median follow-up of 8.1 years. Note explicitly that this is the prespecified final OS analysis, not an interim.

contradictions.quote: A network meta-analysis pooled seven phase III randomised trials, 4,415 patients, at a median follow-up of 73.3 months.
contradictions.counterexample: The Scientific Reports paper (Elliott et al.) reports median follow-up as 70.2 months in the methods/results section (range 48.7–97.2 months), while the abstract states 73.3 months. The draft uses the abstract figure. This is an internal inconsistency in the source paper, but the draft should note which figure it is using and from where.
contradictions.fix: Cite the figure as reported in the abstract of Elliott et al. (73.3 months) and note the methods section reports 70.2 months, or use the more conservative methods-section figure.

contradictions.quote: PALOMA-2 is also the trial whose investigators recorded a large and disproportionate imbalance in missing survival data between its arms, which they said limits interpretation.
contradictions.counterexample: This is fully confirmed and not a contradiction — the ASCO Post, OncLive, and the JCO paper all explicitly report the 13.3% vs 21.2% imbalance and the investigators' own statement that it 'limited interpretation.' The draft's characterisation is accurate and well-supported.
contradictions.fix: No change needed. However, the draft omits the recovered-data sensitivity analysis (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.76–1.12 after data recovery), which still did not reach significance but narrowed the gap. Adding this would strengthen the argument that even correcting for the missing data defect, palbociclib's OS result remains non-significant.

coverage.what_this_piece_can_add: No existing coverage — including the most careful peer-reviewed treatments — connects all three threads simultaneously for a lay reader: (1) that the trials were individually underpowered for OS as a secondary endpoint and the OS discrepancy is statistically expected by chance alone, (2) that the one documented asymmetry between ribociclib and the other two drugs (mandatory cardiac monitoring) runs counter to the direction of the grade, and (3) that the recovered-data PALOMA-2 sensitivity analysis (HR 0.92 after correcting the missing-data imbalance) moves palbociclib's point estimate meaningfully closer to the other two drugs — a fact that further undermines the premise that the OS results reflect stable drug-level differences rather than trial-level artefacts.
